result.investigation_text:
Use the attached list to plan 873 units across 111 products at stores for December 1–7, 2025. Order nothing for the other 225. Check the 56 flagged products at stores first: stock may run short before new orders arrive; consider transfers or faster delivery.

These quantities are illustrative because the supplied stock, delivery and buying rules are marked synthetic. Confirm them before purchasing. Incoming deliveries match the stock records. Quantities subtract stock and incoming deliveries, cover supplier waiting time plus one week, include the supplied reserve, and follow pack sizes and minimum orders.

I recommend averaging the last 13 weeks of recorded orders. Across the same products and weeks, the seasonal alternative reduced weekly errors by about 2% initially—a small difference—but was worse later. No alternative met the agreed consistency requirement. This simple baseline interprets “the last few months”; your exact buying calculation was not supplied, so this does not establish improvement over your process.

The calculation assumes missing entries mean no recorded orders. Empty shelves or missing records could hide demand, so check unusual gaps before buying. Returned orders do not establish stock available for resale. The figures predict recorded orders, not guaranteed availability or savings.

Weekly calculations can run on an ordinary local computer without paid model calls; computer and electricity costs remain. The calculations took about a second. The separate AI-assisted building cost cannot be estimated without usage and pricing information.
